classification.difficultyReason: Identify the π/6 or π/3 reference angle, apply the quadrant signs to sine and cosine, and obtain tangent from their ratio. These are direct applications of taught exact-ratio methods; the repeated columns add no new reasoning demand.

answer.worked:
$\frac{\pi}{6}$ is in quadrant I. The exact $30^\circ$ ratios give $\sin\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac12$ and $\cos\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{\pi}{6}&=\frac{\sin\frac{\pi}{6}}{\cos\frac{\pi}{6}}\\\tan\frac{\pi}{6}&=\frac{\frac12}{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}\\\tan\frac{\pi}{6}&=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\end{aligned}$

$\frac{\pi}{3}$ is in quadrant I. The exact $60^\circ$ ratios give $\sin\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ and $\cos\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac12$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{\pi}{3}&=\frac{\sin\frac{\pi}{3}}{\cos\frac{\pi}{3}}\\\tan\frac{\pi}{3}&=\frac{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}{\frac12}\\\tan\frac{\pi}{3}&=\sqrt3\end{aligned}$

$\frac{2\pi}{3}=\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}$ lies in quadrant II, with reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Sine is positive and cosine is negative, so $\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ and $\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}=-\frac12$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{2\pi}{3}&=\frac{\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}}{\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}}\\\tan\frac{2\pi}{3}&=\frac{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}{-\frac12}\\\tan\frac{2\pi}{3}&=-\sqrt3\end{aligned}$

$\frac{5\pi}{6}=\pi-\frac{\pi}{6}$ lies in quadrant II, with reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$. Sine is positive and cosine is negative, so $\sin\frac{5\pi}{6}=\frac12$ and $\cos\frac{5\pi}{6}=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{5\pi}{6}&=\frac{\sin\frac{5\pi}{6}}{\cos\frac{5\pi}{6}}\\\tan\frac{5\pi}{6}&=\frac{\frac12}{-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}\\\tan\frac{5\pi}{6}&=-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\end{aligned}$

$\frac{7\pi}{6}=\pi+\frac{\pi}{6}$ lies in quadrant III, with reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$. Sine and cosine are negative, so $\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}=-\frac12$ and $\cos\frac{7\pi}{6}=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{7\pi}{6}&=\frac{\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}}{\cos\frac{7\pi}{6}}\\\tan\frac{7\pi}{6}&=\frac{-\frac12}{-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}\\\tan\frac{7\pi}{6}&=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\end{aligned}$

$\frac{4\pi}{3}=\pi+\frac{\pi}{3}$ lies in quadrant III, with reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Sine and cosine are negative, so $\sin\frac{4\pi}{3}=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ and $\cos\frac{4\pi}{3}=-\frac12$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{4\pi}{3}&=\frac{\sin\frac{4\pi}{3}}{\cos\frac{4\pi}{3}}\\\tan\frac{4\pi}{3}&=\frac{-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}{-\frac12}\\\tan\frac{4\pi}{3}&=\sqrt3\end{aligned}$

$\frac{5\pi}{3}=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}$ lies in quadrant IV, with reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Sine is negative and cosine is positive.

$\sin\frac{5\pi}{3}=-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ and $\cos\frac{5\pi}{3}=\frac12$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{5\pi}{3}&=\frac{\sin\frac{5\pi}{3}}{\cos\frac{5\pi}{3}}\\\tan\frac{5\pi}{3}&=\frac{-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}{\frac12}\\\tan\frac{5\pi}{3}&=-\sqrt3\end{aligned}$

$\frac{11\pi}{6}=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{6}$ lies in quadrant IV, with reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$. Sine is negative and cosine is positive.

$\sin\frac{11\pi}{6}=-\frac12$ and $\cos\frac{11\pi}{6}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac{11\pi}{6}&=\frac{\sin\frac{11\pi}{6}}{\cos\frac{11\pi}{6}}\\\tan\frac{11\pi}{6}&=\frac{-\frac12}{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}\\\tan\frac{11\pi}{6}&=-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\end{aligned}$
